questions.question: For $\max\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with slack variables and a basis $\mathcal{B}$, where in the simplex tableau of $\mathcal{B}$ does $\boldsymbol{y}^{\top}=\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ appear?
options: In the constraint rows, under the slack columns
In the objective row, under the structural columns
In the objective row, under the slack columns
In the right-hand side column of the constraint rows

questions.question: For $\max\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with slack variables and a basis $\mathcal{B}$, let $\boldsymbol{y}^{\top}=\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$. Which quantity is the objective-row entry of the tableau of $\mathcal{B}$ in the column of a structural variable $x_j$?
options: $c_j-(\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y})_j$, the shortfall of dual constraint $j$
$(\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y})_j-c_j$, the surplus of dual constraint $j$
$y_j$, the dual variable belonging to the variable $x_j$
$x_j$, the value of $x_j$ in the basic solution of $\mathcal{B}$

questions.question: For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with slack variables, take a basis $\mathcal{B}$, not necessarily optimal, and $\boldsymbol{y}^{\top}=\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$. What does the right-hand side entry of the objective row of its tableau equal?
options: The primal value $Z$; it equals $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$ only when the tableau is optimal
The dual value $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$, which exceeds $Z$ unless the tableau is optimal
The primal value $Z$, while $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$ is the sum of the slack-column entries
Both $Z$ of the basic solution and $W=\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$, for every basis

questions.question: For $\max\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with slack variables and a basis $\mathcal{B}$, let $\boldsymbol{y}^{\top}=\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$. Exactly when is $\boldsymbol{y}$ feasible for the dual linear program?
options: When every objective-row entry, under structural and slack columns, is nonnegative
When every objective-row entry under the slack columns is nonnegative
When every objective-row entry under the structural columns is nonnegative
When every right-hand side entry of the constraint rows is nonnegative

questions.question: For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with slacks $s_1,\dots,s_m$, the tableau of a basis has objective-row entry $-2$ under $s_3$ (a negative entry signals that $Z$ may improve). What does this say about $\boldsymbol{y}^{\top}=\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$?
options: Primal constraint $3$ is violated by $2$ at the basic solution
Dual constraint $3$, $\boldsymbol{A}_3^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq c_3$, is violated by $2$
$y_3=-2$, so $\boldsymbol{y}$ violates $\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$
$y_3=2$, since reduced costs carry the opposite sign

questions.question: For $\max Z=5x_1+4x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq5$, $3x_1+x_2\leq9$, $x_2\leq4$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slacks $s_1,s_2,s_3$, the final simplex tableau has basic variables $x_1=2$, $x_2=3$, $s_3=1$ and objective row $(0,0\mid\frac{7}{2},\frac{1}{2},0\mid22)$ (columns of $x_1,x_2$; of $s_1,s_2,s_3$; right-hand side). What is the optimal dual solution $\boldsymbol{y}$?
options: $\boldsymbol{y}=\left(-\frac{7}{2},-\frac{1}{2},0\right)$
$\boldsymbol{y}=\left(\frac{7}{2},\frac{1}{2},0\right)$
$\boldsymbol{y}=(2,3,1)$
$\boldsymbol{y}=\left(0,0,\frac{7}{2}\right)$

questions.question: For $\max 3x_1+2x_2+4x_3$ subject to $x_1+x_2+2x_3\leq8$, $2x_1+x_2+x_3\leq10$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slacks, the basis $\{x_1,x_2\}$ gives the objective row $(0,0,-1\mid1,1\mid18)$ (columns of $x_1,x_2,x_3$; of the slacks; right-hand side). What does this say about $\boldsymbol{y}=(1,1)$, read under the slack columns?
options: It is dual feasible, since both entries under the slack columns are nonnegative
It satisfies $2y_1+y_2\geq4$ with surplus $1$, the sign being reversed
Nothing: the primal constraint $x_1+x_2+2x_3\leq8$ is violated by $1$
It violates the dual constraint $2y_1+y_2\geq4$ by $1$, so it is infeasible

questions.question: For $\max 4x_1+3x_2+5x_3$ subject to $2x_1+x_2+x_3\leq12$, $x_1+3x_2+2x_3\leq15$, $x_1\leq5$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slacks, the final tableau shows the optimal dual solution $\boldsymbol{y}=(1,2,0)$ under the slack columns. What is its objective-row entry in the column of $x_2$?

For $\max 3x_1+2x_2$ subject to $x_1\leq4$, $x_2\leq3$, $x_1+x_2\leq5$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slacks $s_1,s_2,s_3$, the final simplex tableau has basic variables $x_1=4$, $x_2=1$, $s_2=2$. What is the component $y_2$ of the optimal dual solution read from this tableau?
options: $y_2=2$, the value of $s_2$ in the right-hand side column
$y_2=3$, the right-hand side of the constraint $x_2\leq3$
$y_2=0$, because the basic variable $s_2$ has reduced cost $0$
$y_2$ cannot be found without the objective-row entries

questions.question: The linear program $\min 2x_1+3x_2+x_3$ subject to $x_1+x_2\geq4$, $x_2+x_3\geq3$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ has the dual $\max 4y_1+3y_2$ subject to $y_1\leq2$, $y_1+y_2\leq3$, $y_2\leq1$, $\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$. Each written in standard form with slack variables, which one can the simplex method start from its slack basis, without artificial variables?
options: Only the primal, since it has $2$ constraints and the dual has $3$
Only the dual, since its slack basis has slack values $(2,3,1)\geq\boldsymbol{0}$
Both, once the $\geq$ constraints are multiplied by $-1$ and given slacks
Only the primal, since its slack basis is the origin $\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}$

questions.question: For the linear program $\max\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slack variables $s_1,\dots,s_m$, consider the tableau of a basis $\mathcal{B}$ and $\boldsymbol{y}^{\top}=\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$. Why is the objective-row entry in the column of $s_i$ equal to $y_i$?
options: Slack variables are nonbasic in a final tableau, and the entries of nonbasic variables are the $y_i$
The column of $s_i$ in the tableau is column $i$ of $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$, and the entry is the sum of that column
The cost of $s_i$ in $Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ is $y_i$, so its reduced cost is $y_i$ as well
Its column is $\boldsymbol{e}_i$ with cost $0$, so the entry is $\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{e}_i$

questions.question: In a simplex tableau for $\max\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with slacks, the basic solution $\boldsymbol{x}$ is feasible and no objective-row entry is negative. Why is $\boldsymbol{y}^{\top}=\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ then optimal for the dual linear program?
options: $\boldsymbol{y}$ is dual feasible and $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$, a lower bound on every dual value by weak duality
$\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ and $\boldsymbol{x}$ is primal feasible, so weak duality alone makes $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$ minimal
$\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ holds only at an optimal tableau, and equal values make $\boldsymbol{y}$ optimal
Each simplex pivot lowers the slack-column entries of the objective row, so the final $\boldsymbol{y}$ is minimal

questions.question: For $\max\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with slacks, let $(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{s})$ be the basic solution of a basis and $\boldsymbol{y}^{\top}=\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$. Which holds for $x_j(\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{c})_j$ and $s_iy_i$?
options: They are all zero only if the tableau of $\mathcal{B}$ is optimal
They are all zero for every basis, optimal or not
The products $x_j(\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{c})_j$ vanish, the $s_iy_i$ need not
They are all zero only if the basic solution is nondegenerate

questions.question: For $\max 2x_1+x_2+3x_3$ subject to $x_1+x_2+2x_3\leq10$, $3x_1+x_2+x_3\leq15$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, the optimal basis in the order $(x_3,x_1)$ has $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}=\frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\-1&2\end{bmatrix}$. What is the optimal dual solution $\boldsymbol{y}^{\top}=\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$?
options: $\boldsymbol{y}=\left(\frac{3}{5},\frac{4}{5}\right)$
$\boldsymbol{y}=(3,4)$
$\boldsymbol{y}=\left(\frac{7}{5},\frac{1}{5}\right)$
$\boldsymbol{y}=(7,1)$

questions.question: For $\max Z=2x_1+3x_2$ subject to $x_1+2x_2\leq8$, $3x_1+2x_2\leq12$, $x_1\leq3$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slacks $s_1,s_2,s_3$, take the basis $\{x_2,s_2,s_3\}$, whose basic solution is $\boldsymbol{x}=(0,4)$, $s_2=4$, $s_3=3$, so $Z=12$. What does $\boldsymbol{y}^{\top}=\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ show?
options: Optimal: $\boldsymbol{y}=(\frac{3}{2},0,0)\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, so all slack-column entries are nonnegative
Not optimal: the entry $\frac{3}{2}$ under $s_1$ is positive, so raising $s_1$ raises $Z$
Optimal: $y_2=y_3=0$ matches $s_2,s_3>0$, so complementary slackness holds
Not optimal: $\boldsymbol{y}=(\frac{3}{2},0,0)$ gives $y_1+3y_2+y_3=\frac{3}{2}<2$

questions.question: For $\max Z=4x_1+3x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq6$, $2x_1+x_2\leq10$, $x_1\leq3$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slacks $s_1,s_2,s_3$, the tableau after the first simplex iteration has basic variables $s_1=3$, $s_2=4$, $x_1=3$ and objective row $(0,-3\mid0,0,4\mid12)$ (columns of $x_1,x_2$; of $s_1,s_2,s_3$; right-hand side). What does it show about the optimal value $Z^{\ast}$?
options: $Z^{\ast}\geq12$, but no upper bound: $\boldsymbol{y}=(0,0,4)$ violates $y_1+y_2\geq3$
$Z^{\ast}\leq12$: as $\boldsymbol{y}=(0,0,4)\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, weak duality makes $W=12$ an upper bound
$12\leq Z^{\ast}\leq15$: the entry $-3$ is the most that $Z$ can still gain
Nothing: a tableau with a negative objective-row entry gives no bound on $Z^{\ast}$

questions.question: The program $\min\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ is solved via its dual $\max\{\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\colon\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\leq\boldsymbol{c},\ \boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ by the simplex method. Where does the final tableau show an optimal $\boldsymbol{x}$?
options: In the right-hand side column of the constraint rows, as basic values
In the objective row, under the slack columns of the dual
In the objective row, under the columns of $y_1,\dots,y_m$
Nowhere: the minimization must be solved separately for $\boldsymbol{x}$

questions.question: In a simplex tableau for $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with slacks, no objective-row entry is negative, but some basic variable has a negative value. Which conclusion about $\boldsymbol{y}^{\top}=\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ and the tableau is correct?
options: The basic solution is optimal, since no objective-row entry is negative
The tableau proves $\boldsymbol{y}$ optimal for the dual, since $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$ equals its value $Z$
$\boldsymbol{y}$ is not dual feasible, because the primal basic solution is infeasible
$\boldsymbol{y}$ is dual feasible, so $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$ bounds every feasible primal value from above

questions.question: For $\max x_1+x_2+2x_3$ subject to $3x_1+2x_2+3x_3=8$, $x_1+2x_2+2x_3=6$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ (no slacks), the dual is $\min 8y_1+6y_2$ subject to $3y_1+y_2\geq1$, $2y_1+2y_2\geq1$, $3y_1+2y_2\geq2$, $y_1,y_2$ free. The basis $\{x_2,x_3\}$, with $\boldsymbol{x}=(0,1,2)$, is optimal. What is $\boldsymbol{y}^{\top}=\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$?
options: $\boldsymbol{y}=\left(1,-\frac{1}{2}\right)$
$\boldsymbol{y}=(2,-1)$
$\boldsymbol{y}=\left(1,\frac{1}{2}\right)$
$\boldsymbol{y}=(1,2)$

questions.question: For $\max Z=2x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1\leq1$, $x_1+x_2\leq2$, $x_2\leq1$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slacks $s_1,s_2,s_3$, the basis $\{x_1,x_2,s_1\}$ gives $\boldsymbol{x}=(1,1)$, $s_1=0$ and objective row $(0,0\mid0,2,-1\mid3)$ (columns of $x_1,x_2$; of $s_1,s_2,s_3$; right-hand side). What follows for the dual linear program?
options: Its optimal value exceeds $3$, since the entry $-1$ shows that $\boldsymbol{x}=(1,1)$ is not optimal
$\boldsymbol{y}=(0,2,-1)$ is optimal for it, since $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=3=Z$
$\boldsymbol{y}=(1,1,0)$ is optimal for it, though the tableau gives an infeasible $\boldsymbol{y}$
It has no optimal solution, since the $\boldsymbol{y}$ of this tableau has a negative entry
